chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The hearts are three: an inverted heart that does not grasp any good, and it is the heart of the disbeliever; and a heart in which is a black spot, so good and evil wrestle in it, and whichever of the two prevails over it, it dominates; and an open heart in which are shining lamps, and its light will not be extinguished until the Day of Resurrection, and it is the heart of the believer.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of hearts described in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the spiritual anatomy of the heart (qalb) into three distinct states: the inverted heart of the disbeliever devoid of good, the mixed heart of the hypocrite where good and evil contend, and the radiant, open heart of the believer illuminated until Judgment Day. Scholarly tradition interprets the 'black spot' in the hypocrite's heart as the locus of spiritual conflict, reflecting the Shi'a emphasis on the internal reality of faith beyond mere verbal profession. The enduring light of the believer's heart underscores the concept of divine illumination (nur) that persists through the trials of worldly life.
